# Research Summary: Stiles v. Pinecrest — Advancement of Defense Costs

## Short Answers

1. **Entitlement.** Yes as to **Count I** (fiduciary duty as CFO) — squarely "by reason of the fact" of his office. **No as to Count II** (failure to deliver 2025 consulting services) — a purely personal contractual obligation incurred after he left office. **Count III is a close call**; our view is that it is at least partly covered because Pinecrest must prove he acquired the pricing data as CFO, with allocation of any purely contractual work.
2. **Bylaw amendment.** Not effective against him. §145(f) bars post-conduct impairment of a bylaw advancement right unless the original provision reserved that power; the 2019 bylaw did not, and all alleged conduct (2023–June 2025) predates the August 12, 2025 amendment.
3. **Conditions.** No on both. Good faith is irrelevant to advancement (it is an indemnification question), and the bylaw itself requires only an *unsecured* undertaking.
4. **Enforcement/fees.** Summary proceeding in the Delaware Court of Chancery (exclusive jurisdiction). Fees on fees are recoverable in proportion to success because the bylaw grants rights "to the fullest extent permitted by law."

## Analysis

### 1. Which claims are advanceable

The 2019 bylaw [4] is mandatory ("shall… advance"), reaches persons who "is or was" an officer, and covers any Proceeding "brought by reason of the fact" of that status. §145(e) [1] authorizes exactly this. The dispositive question is the "by reason of the fact" nexus, which under *Doe* [5] turns on whether the claim connects to the person's corporate powers or duties; purely personal or contractual obligations are excluded, and mixed claims are allocated.

- **Count I** alleges Stiles breached fiduciary duties *as CFO* by overstating bookings in 2023–24. The claim exists only because he held the office. Covered.
- **Count II** alleges non-performance of transition services under a Consulting Agreement he signed individually, after his tenure ended. The duty arises from the contract, not his office. Not covered under [5]. We should not press this count; it would dilute our fees-on-fees recovery (see §4).
- **Count III** is mixed. Pinecrest frames it as breach of a contractual confidentiality clause (personal, 2025), but the claim depends on proving the data was "learned as CFO" — i.e., acquired by virtue of his corporate position. *Our view:* there is a sufficient nexus to his official capacity to support advancement, at minimum for work addressing how and in what capacity he obtained the information. *Strongest counter:* the breached duty is contractual, the breach occurred when he was a consultant, and a merely historical connection to his former office is not a nexus to the *exercise* of corporate powers — otherwise any post-employment claim against a former officer would be covered. Expect the Court to allocate; we should propose a protocol under which work serving both Count I and Count III is advanced in full and only Count III–specific contractual work is excluded or allocated.

Also confirm the bylaws' definition of "Covered Person" includes former officers (the operative sentence's "is or was" language strongly suggests so).

### 2. The August 2025 amendment

§145(f) [2] provides that a bylaw advancement right "shall not be eliminated or impaired" by a later amendment adopted "after the occurrence of the act or omission that is the subject of the… proceeding," unless the provision in effect at the time "explicitly authorizes" such impairment. The 2019 text contains no such reservation [4]. The conduct underlying Count I (2023–24) and Count III (January–June 2025) all predates August 12, 2025. The amendment therefore cannot convert his mandatory right into a discretionary one for this suit. The statute keys to the *act or omission*, not the filing date, so the fact that Pinecrest sued in October 2025 is irrelevant.

Pinecrest's position tracks the 2004 treatise [8] ("at any time before a claim is asserted"). That statement predates the current text of §145(f) and is superseded. *Strongest counter:* Pinecrest may argue the "fullest extent permitted by law" phrase incorporates whatever bylaw the Board has in force. This fails: §145(f) is precisely a limit on what the Board may do after the fact, and the phrase expands rather than contracts the right.

### 3. Good-faith precondition and letter of credit

*Roe* [6] holds advancement does not depend on the merits or the officer's good faith; those questions are reserved for indemnification at final disposition. That is consistent with §145(e) [1], which conditions advancement only on an undertaking to repay if the officer is "ultimately" found not entitled to indemnification. The 2016 blog post [7] states the contrary but cites nothing and is inconsistent with [1] and [6]; it should not be relied on.

On security: §145(e) requires only an "undertaking," and Pinecrest's own bylaw specifies an "*unsecured* undertaking to repay" [4]. Pinecrest cannot graft a letter-of-credit requirement onto a right it drafted without one; and because the amended bylaw is ineffective under §145(f) (§2 above), the Board's "sole discretion" language cannot supply that authority either. *Counter:* Pinecrest will stress that §145(e) is permissive ("may"), so corporations can impose conditions. True in the abstract, but the only operative conditions are those in the governing bylaw, and the bylaw forecloses security.

### 4. Enforcement and fees on fees

§145(k) [3] gives the Court of Chancery exclusive jurisdiction and authorizes it to "summarily determine" the advancement obligation. We should (i) deliver a written demand enclosing Stiles's executed unsecured undertaking and invoices (redacted for privilege), and (ii) if Pinecrest does not pay within a short deadline, file a verified complaint with a motion for expedition/summary adjudication.

Under *Doe* [5], fees incurred in the advancement action are recoverable "in proportion to success" where the bylaw grants rights "to the fullest extent permitted by law" — Pinecrest's does [4]. This argues for a disciplined demand: seek Counts I and III, concede Count II, and propose a reasonable allocation mechanism up front so that our success ratio is high.

## Source Reliability

| # | Source | Weight | Notes |
|---|--------|--------|-------|
| 1 | 8 Del. C. §145(e) | High — controlling statute | Excerpt only; confirm current text. |
| 2 | 8 Del. C. §145(f) | High — controlling statute | Dispositive on amendment issue. Confirm current text. |
| 3 | 8 Del. C. §145(k) | High — controlling statute | Governs forum and summary procedure. |
| 4 | Pinecrest bylaws Art. VII §2 | High — governing instrument | Need full Article VII, "Covered Person" definition, certificate of incorporation, and any indemnification agreement. |
| 5 | *Doe v. Alder Systems* (Del. Ch.) | Medium-high | Flagged as fictional for this exercise; must be replaced with/verified against real Delaware authority before filing. |
| 6 | *Roe v. Example Holdings* (Del. Ch.) | Medium-high | Same caveat as [5]. |
| 7 | Law-firm blog (2016) | Low | Unsourced, dated, contradicts [1] and [6]. Do not cite. |
| 8 | Treatise (2004 ed.) | Low on this point | Predates current §145(f); superseded. Useful only to anticipate Pinecrest's argument. |

## Next Steps

1. Obtain the complete bylaws (all amendments), certificate of incorporation, any indemnification agreement, the Consulting Agreement (check for indemnification, fee-shifting, or forum clauses), and Board minutes for the August 12, 2025 amendment.
2. Confirm the "Covered Person" definition and that the amendment was not accompanied by any purported ratification language targeting Stiles.
3. Pull and verify current Delaware authority on (a) "by reason of the fact" for confidentiality claims by former officers and (b) allocation protocols for mixed claims; replace [5]/[6] with citable decisions.
4. Send demand with executed unsecured undertaking, invoices, and a proposed allocation protocol; set a 10-business-day deadline.
5. Tender notice to Pinecrest's D&O carrier (Side A) in parallel.
6. Prepare a verified Chancery complaint and motion to expedite under §145(k), seeking advancement for Counts I and III plus fees on fees.
